title: Traveling with Friends Expect to Fight over Costs!
paragraphs: A vacation with friends sounds like a lot of fun. But according to a new survey, money can cause problems, and many people would rather pay more than argue.

The survey was carried out online by the Harris Poll in May 2026 for CIT Bank, an American bank. It asked 2,067 adults in the United States about group travel. More than half of them, 54%, had taken a trip with friends or family members who do not live with them in the past five years.

Of these group travelers, 45% said that they had experienced arguments or felt uncomfortable about money on a trip. Young people had the most problems. Among Gen Z travelers, aged 18 to 29, the number was 72%. And 22% of them said they had ended a relationship because of money problems on a group trip.

To avoid arguments, many people are willing to pay extra. In the survey, 82% said they would pay more than their fair share to avoid a fight about money. The bank calls this a "peace tax." In fact, 21% of millennials, aged 30 to 45, said they would pay more than $500 extra.

Many people also feel pressure to travel. For example, 41% said they had felt pressure to go on a trip that they did not want to go on. In addition, 61% of group travelers said they had spent more than their budget because of pressure from other people.
Weddings can be especially expensive. Among people who went to a wedding or a party before a wedding in the past five years, 59% spent more than $1,000 on travel for these events.
Jose Castro, the head of CIT Bank, said that traveling with a group "should feel like a joy, not a financial calculation." The bank suggests saving money for group trips before they happen.
